skill.name: hubspot-integration
skill.description: Practical HubSpot CRM integration patterns for authentication, object operations, associations, batching, webhooks, and custom objects with Node.js and Python.
skill.summary: Build HubSpot CRM integrations with authentication, data management, batching, associations, webhooks, and custom objects.

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives involving expected HubSpot API requests, scoped environment variables, JavaScript interpolation, and CRM identifier mapping. However, the OAuth example omits state validation, and the webhook example does not implement HubSpot signature v3 correctly.

remediation.issue: The OAuth authorization flow does not create or validate a state value.
remediation.suggestion: Generate a cryptographically random state value, bind it to the user session, and validate it before exchanging the authorization code.

remediation.issue: The webhook handler labels its check as signature v3 but applies an incompatible body-only HMAC algorithm.
remediation.suggestion: Use the raw body, method, decoded URI, and timestamp for v3 verification. Compare the Base64 HMAC with a timing-safe function.

semantic_findings.title: OAuth State Validation Is Missing
semantic_findings.description: The authorization URL omits a random state parameter, and the callback exchanges a code without validating state. This permits OAuth login CSRF or account misbinding.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The complete authorization URL and callback example shows no state generation, session binding, or validation.

semantic_findings.title: HubSpot Signature v3 Verification Is Incorrect
semantic_findings.description: The handler reads the v3 header but verifies a hex HMAC over only the serialized body. HubSpot v3 requires additional request data, Base64 output, and timing-safe comparison.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example explicitly reads the v3 signature and timestamp, but the HMAC covers only JSON.stringify(req.body) and uses direct string equality.

content.value_statement: HubSpot integrations require careful authentication, object handling, pagination, and webhook processing. This skill provides practical Node.js and Python patterns for common CRM workflows.
actual_capabilities: Drafts OAuth 2.0 and private app authentication flows for HubSpot.
Creates examples for contact CRUD, search, pagination, and batch operations.
Models associations between contacts, companies, and deals with Associations v4.
Outlines webhook receipt, signature checks, timestamp checks, and asynchronous processing.
Defines custom object schemas and record operations.
Highlights rate limits, token rotation, deprecations, and validation checks.
limitations: Examples require adaptation to the installed HubSpot SDK version and application framework.
Credentials, scopes, portal permissions, queues, storage, and deployment infrastructure are not provided.
Custom objects require an eligible HubSpot Enterprise subscription.
Security-sensitive examples require review because the included OAuth state and webhook v3 verification patterns are incomplete.

use_cases.title: Synchronize CRM contacts
use_cases.description: Design contact creation, updates, searches, pagination, and batches for an application integration.

use_cases.title: Configure an internal CRM connection
use_cases.description: Plan a private app integration with scoped access, token handling, associations, and rate-limit controls.

use_cases.title: Review webhook ingestion
use_cases.description: Assess signature verification, replay protection, response timing, and queued event processing before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Connect a private app
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Node.js HubSpot private app client using an environment variable. Add paginated contact retrieval and bounded rate-limit retries.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one HubSpot account

prompt_templates.title: Build contact synchronization
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a contact synchronization workflow for these source fields: [fields]. Include search, create, update, batching, pagination, and partial-failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Implement secure webhooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Express HubSpot webhook handler. Verify signature v3 using the raw body, method, URI, and timestamp. Add replay protection and queuing.

prompt_templates.title: Architect a multi-account integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-account HubSpot integration for [requirements]. Cover OAuth state, token rotation, scopes, associations, custom objects, throttling, observability, and recovery.

output_examples.input: Create a private app contact reader with pagination.
output_examples.output: A Node.js implementation plan that loads a named token, requests selected properties, follows cursors, and retries bounded rate-limit responses.
A security checklist covering raw-body preservation, signature v3 inputs, timing-safe comparison, timestamp freshness, fast responses, and asynchronous event processing.

output_examples.input: Plan a project custom object linked to contacts and companies.
output_examples.output: A schema plan with required properties, field types, supported associations, record operations, search behavior, and Enterprise subscription constraints.

best_practices: Request only required HubSpot scopes and keep tokens in a managed secret store.
Implement cursor pagination, bounded retries, and rate-limit backoff for every list or bulk workflow.
Validate OAuth state and HubSpot webhook v3 signatures against raw request data before processing.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode private app tokens, OAuth client secrets, or access tokens.
Do not process webhook payloads before authenticating the signature and checking timestamp freshness.
Do not issue unbounded parallel requests or ignore pagination and partial batch failures.

faq.question: Does this skill execute HubSpot requests?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation patterns that require your credentials, application code, permissions, and testing.

faq.question: Should I use OAuth or a private app token?
faq.answer: Use OAuth for multiple customer accounts. Use a private app token for one controlled HubSpot account.

faq.question: Which SDKs are covered?
faq.answer: The examples primarily use the HubSpot Node.js SDK and include a limited Python authentication example.

faq.question: Does it cover webhook security?
faq.answer: It discusses signatures and replay checks, but the included v3 verification example needs correction before production use.

faq.question: Can it define HubSpot custom objects?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers schema creation and record operations, subject to HubSpot Enterprise limits and permissions.

faq.question: Does it handle rate limits and pagination?
faq.answer: It provides patterns for cursor pagination, batching, delays, and retry handling. Production systems still need monitoring and bounded retries.
